title: Activation gain matcher: runtime adapter and calibration harness for INT8 deploys
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: We see intermittent accuracy regressions when deploying INT8 profiles generated by offline calibrators into the runtime. Root cause analysis shows two main factors: (1) drift in activation distributions between calibration instrumentation (micro-batches with observer hooks) and real production batching/sequence-length slices; (2) slight numeric mismatches between the pre-trained model's calibration scale factors and fused/inlined kernel math (kernel reorder, fused gelu, and cast placement).

Proposed solution: Implement an 'activation gain matcher' runtime adapter plus a CI-friendly calibration harness. The adapter sits between model metadata and kernel dispatcher: it loads per-layer gain-correction tables produced by a new calibration pass, applies deterministic rescaling to activation ranges at dispatch time (before kernel quantization path), and exposes a compact profile format (binary + JSON manifest) that the runtime can reload without restarting. The calibration harness will: capture production-like slices (sequence length distribution, prefix contexts), run micro-batch calibration with online KV cache simulation, compute layer-wise gain deltas relative to the training instrumentation baseline, and emit a signed gain-profile. We will also add a kernel shim to accept a per-invocation correction factor and a safe FP16 fallback when correction exceeds a threshold.

Why this is different from previous work: rather than re-tuning quantization parameters or modifying the calibration algorithm itself, this approach accepts the offline INT8 profile and introduces a small, verifiable runtime correction that prevents regressions while keeping the original profile's unit-cost advantages. It bridges the gap between calibration-time assumptions and production runtime realities (batching, kernel fusions, and caching).

Risk profile: low-to-medium implementation risk for the adapter and profile format; medium risk for kernel shims (must preserve latency SLOs). The FP16 fallback threshold needs careful tuning to avoid frequent fallbacks that increase cost.

Artifacts: Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/QUANT/Activation+Gain+Matcher+Spec; prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3748; calibration harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quant-calib-harness; eval dashboard (internal): https://dashboards.redwood.ai/quant/70123-gain-matcher
acceptance_criteria: Runtime adapter can load compact gain-profile and apply per-layer rescaling at kernel dispatch with <1% median latency regression
Calibration harness produces reproducible gain-profile binaries and a human-readable manifest
Integration test demonstrates <0.5% top-1/LM perplexity regression on Golden Prompt Set compared to FP16 baseline for the tested model family
Kernel shim supports safe FP16 fallback when gain-correction > configured threshold and exposes metrics for fallback rate
End-to-end CI job fails on model-side accuracy regression > 1% and uploads diff artifacts to the eval dashboard

2025-02-28 - Priya Raman (SRE): CI runner resource requirement noted: the harness needs KV-cache sim which increases memory footprint. Suggest adding a 'calib-lite' mode to reduce memory for nightly runs.
